correctness_confidence.basis: Every step of Theorems 1 and 2 was checked algebraically and verified; the n=3 correlation minor formula D2(u), all exact integer permanents, ||w||_2^2 values, gaps, Rayleigh ratios, spectral ratios, and Re-stripped ratios for the printed n=8, 9, 10 witnesses (cert08, cert09, cert11) in Theorem 3 and Table 1 were independently verified in exact arithmetic against direct Ryser permanents and the Cauchy-Binet ESP formula.

novelty.basis: Establishes the exact O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet elementary-symmetric-polynomial Gram factorization of F_A at rank 2, the n=3 shift-Laplacian identity reducing 3x3 Bapat-Sunder to rank <= 2, the closed-form n-th root circulant Fourier spectrum with its AM-GM barrier (n-1)^(-1/n) < 1, and the first explicit rank-2 complex counterexamples (including the ultra-compact J_9 + z_9 z_9^* witness at n=9 and high-margin witness at n=10).

reproducibility.basis: Three of the four refutation witnesses (cert08 at n=8, cert09 at n=9, cert11 at n=10) are printed entry-by-entry in the PDF and are immediately and independently verifiable from the manuscript alone. Minor deduction because the explicit vectors for the fourth Table 1 witness (cert10) and the Lean/Python artifacts reside in the linked repository rather than in the PDF.

rigor.basis: Prose proofs for all general-n statements (Theorem 1(a)-(c), Theorem 2(a)-(d)) are complete, tight, and free of gaps, and Section 5 honestly separates the finite-n Lean 4.36.0 kernel proofs and evaluations from the general-n analytic proofs and the unproved numerical observation of no rank-2 complex violations for 4 <= n <= 7.

significance.basis: Resolves the minimal nontrivial rank (rank 2, since rank 1 is identically rigid) at which complex phases break the Bapat-Sunder inequality, explains structurally why naive optimization stalls on the trivial eigenvalue per(A) along 1 and why circulant symmetry cannot violate the bound, and introduces an O(n^3) algebraic framework for rank-2 permanent cofactor matrices.

summary: The paper resolves the rank-2 Hermitian positive semidefinite regime of the 1985 Bapat-Sunder conjecture (per(A)I_n - F_A >= 0, where F_A = A o adj_per(A)). Theorem 1 establishes the universal row-sum eigenpair F_A 1 = per(A) 1 (reducing Bapat-Sunder to lambda_max(F_A|_{1^perp}) <= per(A)), exact diagonal congruence invariance rendering F_A/per(A) a projective invariant on (CP^1)^n at rank 2, and an exact O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet elementary-symmetric-polynomial (ESP) Gram factorization proving F_A >= 0 unconditionally at rank 2. Theorem 2 establishes exact n=2 rigidity, an exact n=3 shift-Laplacian identity reducing 3x3 Hermitian Bapat-Sunder to rank <= 2 (where F_{A_0}|_{1^perp} collapses to an explicit rank-2 operator), the exact Fourier spectrum of F_{A_n(r)} on n-th roots of unity proving sup_{r>0} lambda_max(F_{A_n(r)}|_{1^perp})/per(A_n(r)) = (n-1)^(-1/n) < 1 for all n >= 3, and exact boundary saturation (=1) on real balanced direct sums 2(J_m + J_m). Theorem 3 exhibits explicit Gaussian-integer rank-2 complex counterexamples at n=8, n=9 (including A_9 = J_9 + z_9 z_9^*), and n=10 (Rayleigh ratio > 1.08557, spectral ratio ~1.09508), showing that stripping imaginary parts restores <= 1 on all witnesses. Independent exact-arithmetic checks confirm all printed proofs, identities, Table 1 figures, and witnesses.
strengths: Exact O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet ESP Gram factorization (Theorem 1(c)) makes rank-2 permanent cofactor analysis algebraically transparent, proves F_A >= 0 immediately, and enables zero-float exact verification over Z[i].

Sharp structural diagnostics (Theorem 1(a) row-sum eigenpair and Theorem 2(c) circulant AM-GM barrier (n-1)^(-1/n) < 1) explain both why naive optimization stalls at 1 and why breaking phase/radial symmetry is necessary.
Clean n=3 shift-Laplacian identity (Theorem 2(b)) gives a direct algebraic reduction of the 3x3 Bapat-Sunder theorem to rank <= 2.

Explicit, independently verified Gaussian-integer counterexamples at n=8, 9, 10—especially the ultra-compact s=1 matrix J_9 + z_9 z_9^* (per(A_9) = 6,088,320) and the >8.55% margin s=2 witness at n=10.
Exemplary transparency in Section 5 regarding verification scope, cleanly distinguishing Lean-checked finite identities/evaluations from general-n prose proofs and numerical search bounds.
weaknesses: Explicit vector entries for the second n=9 witness (cert10 in Table 1) are omitted from the manuscript text and available only in the external repository, although the other three witnesses (cert08, cert09, cert11) are printed in full and already suffice for Theorem 3.

Whether n=8 is provably the minimal dimension for rank-2 complex violations remains open analytically: non-violation for rank-2 complex matrices in dimensions 4 <= n <= 7 (and rank-2 real matrices up to n=16) is supported only by multi-start numerical optimization.
Minor notational polish issues: in Theorem 2(b), the Bargmann phase theta in u = P cos(theta) and the matrix M in the proof's M_11 M_22 - |M_12|^2 are left implicit from context.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet ESP Gram factorization of F_A = A o adj_per(A) for rank-2 PSD matrices (Theorem 1(c)).
Exact n=3 shift-Laplacian identity per(A_0 + t I_3)I_3 - F_{A_0 + t I_3} = (per(A_0)I_3 - F_{A_0}) + t L(|A_0|^{o2}) and rank-2 1^perp spectral collapse (Theorem 2(b)).
Exact n-th root circulant Fourier spectrum of F_{A_n(r)} and universal AM-GM barrier (n-1)^(-1/n) < 1 (Theorem 2(c)).
Explicit zero-float Gaussian-integer rank-2 complex counterexamples to the Bapat-Sunder conjecture at n=8, 9, 10 (Theorem 3).
